title: Inside the Cold Chain Network Powering Lacrem’s Growth
summary: The post Inside the Cold Chain Network Powering Lacrem’s Growth appeared first on Americold .
body_text: July is National Ice Cream Month, a celebration of one of the world’s favorite frozen treats. While consumers celebrated by enjoying their favorite flavors and brands, few see the temperature-controlled supply chain working behind the scenes to keep products moving from production to freezer aisles. For more than 20 years, Americold has partnered with Lacrem , parent company of the iconic La Menorquina ice cream brand, helping support its growth across Spain and into international markets, including the United Kingdom and the United States. The recent extension of our partnership through 2029 reflects two decades of collaboration and a shared commitment to future growth. Building a Supply Chain Designed for Growth As Lacrem has continued to expand its business, including achieving consecutive years of double-digit growth and growing its presence in international markets, it needed a supply chain that could scale alongside its ambitions. Supporting that growth requires more than cold storage capacity. It requires an integrated logistics network designed to keep products moving efficiently, reliably, and at scale. To help meet those needs, Americold provides a cold chain solution that combines strategic infrastructure, automation, and supply chain expertise across Spain. A Centralized Hub in Barcelona The journey begins at Americold’s facility in Santa Perpètua de Mogoda, Barcelona , where 100% of Lacrem’s inventory is centralized. Serving as the heart of the operation, the facility manages large-scale frozen storage and precise case-picking activities that support national distribution. By consolidating inventory in a strategically located hub, Lacrem can efficiently manage product flow while maintaining visibility and control across its network. Automation Designed to Keep Products Moving Once orders are ready for shipment, automation helps accelerate product flow and improve operational efficiency. Americold’s automated pallet preparation process retrieves and transports pallets to specialized staging areas, where loads are optimized and prepared for shipment. Products then move directly to cross-dock zones for truck loading and outbound distribution. By combining automation with operational expertise, Americold helps streamline the movement of temperature-sensitive products while supporting the speed and reliability that growing food manufacturers require. Building Supply Chain Resilience in Valencia While Barcelona serves as the primary operating hub, Americold’s facility in Valencia provides an additional layer of resilience. The dedicated safety stock facility helps de-risk regional supply lines and protect product availability throughout the Levante region and southern distribution routes. This strategic inventory positioning enables greater flexibility while helping ensure continuity of supply when demand fluctuates. A Partnership Built for the Future Together, Americold’s strategically located facilities, advanced automation capabilities, and integrated logistics expertise create a cold chain network designed to support Lacrem’s continued growth. The recent extension of the partnership through 2029 marks another milestone in a relationship built on mutual trust, operational excellence, and a shared commitment to delivering results. As Lacrem continues to expand its reach, Americold remains focused on providing the infrastructure, technology, and expertise needed to help keep products moving efficiently from production to point of sale. As food manufacturers navigate growth, changing consumer demand, and increasingly complex supply chains, Americold provides the cold chain solutions needed to scale with confidence. Learn more about Americold’s solutions for producers: https://www.americold.com/producers/ .

title: The Value of Biosensing for Preventative Medicine | Michael Dubrovsky & Josh Clemente
body_text: Biosensing offers people real-time insight into their health status. Regular insight, rather than one-time results at an annual checkup, helps people assess how lifestyle factors are impacting their health, whether they need to make adjustments, and which adjustments might have the most impact. Michael Dubrovsky and Josh Clemente discuss the value of biosensing and how it has the potential to disrupt the healthcare industry, shifting from a diagnose-and-treat approach to a preventive and actionable approach. Listen to the podcast here .

title: Kecil Tapi Bersemangat: Putrajaya Mulakan Juara Digital Pandai 2026
summary: Juara Digital Pandai Putrajaya bermula di SMK Putrajaya Presint 8(1) dengan 28 sekolah dan sokongan MPOC sebagai penaja utama program.
body_text: Putrajaya, Wilayah Persekutuan — Majlis Pelancaran Juara Digital Pandai Kebangsaan (JDP) 2026 Peringkat SSTP Putrajaya berlangsung penuh makna. Perasmi majlis, Puan Alawiah binti Muhammad Hussain, merasmikan acara sejurus selepas memulakan tugas baharu sebagai Timbalan Pengarah Perancangan, Jabatan Pendidikan WP Putrajaya. Lebih menarik, majlis ini turut disokong oleh Malaysian Palm Oil Council (MPOC) sebagai penaja utama program. Majlis berlangsung pada 25 Jun 2026 di SMK Putrajaya Presint 8(1). Secara keseluruhan, ia menghimpunkan 28 buah sekolah — 16 sekolah rendah dan 12 sekolah menengah . Walaupun bilangannya lebih kecil berbanding negeri lain, momentumnya tetap kuat. Malah, mesej jelas daripada perasmi sendiri menjadikan majlis ini lebih bermakna. MPOC Kekal Penaja Utama, Kali Ini Menerusi Skrin Berbeza sedikit daripada peluncuran negeri lain, wakil rasmi MPOC tidak hadir secara fizikal di Putrajaya. Namun, MPOC tetap kekal sebagai penaja utama JDP 2026. Kehadiran mereka dibawa menerusi dua cara: Bunting rasmi MPOC di sekitar lokasi majlis Tayangan video kolaborasi MPOC x Upin & Ipin — Edisi Minyak Sawit Tayangan video ini menjadi cara paling berkesan untuk menyampaikan mesej industri sawit kepada murid. Sebagai contoh, watak kartun yang mereka kenali digunakan untuk menerangkan kepentingan industri sawit. Hasilnya, mesej tersebut menjadi lebih mudah difahami. Perasmi Baharu, Arahan Jelas: Gunakan Pandai Seiring Era Digital Salah satu sorotan utama majlis ialah ucapan perasmian Puan Alawiah binti Muhammad Hussain. Uniknya, beliau baru sahaja memulakan tugas sebagai Timbalan Pengarah Perancangan pada hari yang sama. Dalam ucapannya, beliau menyampaikan komitmen yang jelas. Menurut beliau, beliau akan terus mendesak setiap sekolah di Putrajaya untuk menggunakan Pandai, selari dengan keperluan dunia digital masa kini. Arahan ini datang terus daripada pegawai yang baru memulakan tugas. Justeru, ia menunjukkan keutamaan beliau sejak hari pertama. Di samping itu, permulaan baharu seorang pegawai ini bertepatan dengan permulaan baharu sekolah-sekolah Putrajaya dalam JDP 2026. Hasilnya, detik ini terasa lebih bermakna berbanding majlis rasmi biasa. 28 Sekolah, Padat Dengan Penglibatan Majlis ini menyasarkan penyertaan sekolah rendah dan menengah di seluruh Putrajaya. Secara keseluruhan, peluncuran ini melibatkan: 28 sekolah keseluruhan 16 sekolah rendah 12 sekolah menengah Selain penyertaan sekolah, majlis turut dihadiri: 1 Timbalan Pengarah 4 wakil SSTP 1 wakil SIP 1 wakil SISC 1 pegawai Sektor Pengurusan Bakat (SPB) 1 pegawai pendidikan Islam 2 urus setia sekolah (guru) 4 pentadbir sekolah 4 wakil VIP Pandai Tambahan pula, seramai 100 murid SMK Putrajaya Presint 8(1) hadir selaku tuan rumah. Hasilnya, suasana majlis menjadi lebih hidup sepanjang acara. Dirasmikan Oleh Pegawai Yang Baru Mula Bertugas Detik ini menjadi lebih istimewa kerana satu sebab. Perasmi majlis, Puan Alawiah, baru sahaja memulakan tugas dalam jawatannya pada hari yang sama. Justeru, permulaan baharu seorang pegawai pendidikan bertemu dengan permulaan baharu sekolah-sekolah Putrajaya dalam JDP 2026. Malah, gandingan dua permulaan ini menjadikan majlis terasa lebih bermakna berbanding acara rasmi biasa. Pengisian Acara Yang Padat Dan Bermakna Majlis berlangsung dengan pengisian yang tersusun. Ia bermula dengan ketibaan peserta dan sesi pendaftaran. Seterusnya, majlis diteruskan dengan nyanyian lagu kebangsaan dan bacaan doa. Selepas itu, tayangan video MPOC x Upin & Ipin diputarkan sebagai wakil kehadiran penaja utama. Kemudian, ucapan perasmian disampaikan oleh Puan Alawiah. Suasana majlis diperkukuh dengan gimik peluncuran. Menariknya, gimik ini dilakukan bersama oleh Puan Alawiah, pengetua sekolah tuan rumah, dan En. Suhaimi Ramly selaku Ketua Pegawai Operasi (COO) Pandai. Akhirnya, majlis diteruskan dengan sesi taklimat pelaksanaan JDP 2026, cabutan bertuah, dan penyerahan bahan promosi kepada sekolah. Taklimat Pelaksanaan JDP 2026 Kepada Sekolah Sesi taklimat menjadi antara bahagian paling penting. Di sinilah sekolah diberi penerangan lebih jelas tentang pelaksanaan Juara Digital Pandai 2026. Sesi ini disampaikan oleh Pengarah Pandai sendiri, iaitu En. Zulfaqar Rosli. Antara fokus utama taklimat ialah: mekanisme pertandingan garis masa program ganjaran dan insentif untuk sekolah peluang penyertaan pelajar penglibatan aktif sekolah dalam menggerakkan murid Melalui taklimat ini, sekolah Putrajaya bukan sahaja menerima maklumat asas. Malah, mereka dapat melihat dengan lebih jelas bagaimana JDP 2026 boleh digerakkan secara tersusun di sekolah masing-masing. Tentang Juara Digital Pandai 2026 Juara Digital Pandai 2026 ialah pertandingan akademik digital dalam aplikasi Pandai. Ia terbuka kepada pelajar Malaysia berumur 7 hingga 17 tahun. Butiran utama pertandingan: Tempoh pertandingan: 1 Mei – 31 Ogos 2026 Grand Finale: 19 September 2026 Hadiah terkumpul: RM350,000 Pendaftaran: Percuma Kategori: Sekolah Rendah dan Sekolah Menengah Secara ringkas, pelajar akan belajar dalam aplikasi Pandai dan mengumpul Pandai Score. Selain itu, mereka bermain JDP Game, mendapatkan Ruby, serta naik tier dan leaderboard. Akhirnya, mereka mengumpul GF Points untuk peluang mara ke Grand Finale. Tonton Semula Kemeriahan Majlis Nak rasai sendiri suasana majlis? Tonton video highlight di bawah. Dalam masa beberapa minit sahaja, anda dapat melihat detik-detik penting sepanjang acara. Juara Digital Pandai Putrajaya Buktikan Saiz Bukan Penentu Semangat Bilangan sekolah di Putrajaya memang tidak sebanyak negeri lain. Namun, mesej yang dibawa perasmi sudah cukup jelas — setiap sekolah perlu bergerak dengan Pandai, tidak kira besar atau kecil bilangannya. Dengan sokongan MPOC, gimik yang turut melibatkan pihak teknikal Pandai, serta semangat 100 murid tuan rumah, JDP 2026 di Putrajaya bermula dengan padat dan penuh makna. Jadi, soalannya sekarang — dengan arahan terus daripada perasmi sendiri, berapa ramai lagi sekolah di Putrajaya akan mula bergerak dengan Pandai selepas ini? Layari go.pandai.org/juaradigital untuk maklumat lanjut dan pendaftaran.

title: Severe Flooding in Northern China Leaves Communities Facing Massive Losses, Unsafe Homes, and Livestock Disaster
summary: Flood Aftermath Creates New Challenges for Residents in Jilin Province Communities in northern China’s Jilin Province are facing serious challenges after days of heavy rainfall and flooding damaged homes, destroyed farmland, and caused widespread losses for residents and local businesses. As floodwaters gradually disappeared from affected areas, residents reported scenes of destruction, including abandoned vehicles, unsafe buildings, damaged agricultural land, and large numbers of dead animals
body_text: Flood Aftermath Creates New Challenges for Residents in Jilin Province Communities in northern China’s Jilin Province are facing serious challenges after days of heavy rainfall and flooding damaged homes, destroyed farmland, and caused widespread losses for residents and local businesses. As floodwaters gradually disappeared from affected areas, residents reported scenes of destruction, including abandoned vehicles, unsafe buildings, damaged agricultural land, and large numbers of dead animals left behind. The flooding affected areas including Dunhua City and nearby towns, where residents said the impact extended beyond temporary water damage. Many families are now struggling with housing problems, economic losses, and uncertainty about how they will rebuild their lives. Heavy Rainfall and Reservoir Discharges Linked to Rising Water Levels According to local accounts, continuous rainfall began affecting Jilin Province in mid-July 2026. Residents reported that water levels increased rapidly after multiple reservoirs released floodwaters, contributing to severe flooding in several areas. Jilin Province reportedly contains more than 100 large and medium-sized reservoirs, while Dunhua City has numerous smaller reservoirs spread across surrounding areas. Residents said flooding began quickly in some villages, leaving little time for preparation. Zhou Huijuan, a villager from Shaheyan Town in Dunhua City, described the event as one of the most difficult experiences she had faced. She said floodwaters entered the area during the evening, affecting several nearby villages. Many homes in rural parts of northeastern China are single-story structures, making them particularly vulnerable during major floods. According to her account, some houses were almost completely covered, with only rooftops visible in areas where the water was shallower. Other buildings disappeared beneath deeper floodwaters. Homes Declared Unsafe After Floodwaters Recede Although the water levels eventually dropped, the damage left behind created new dangers for residents. Many rural houses were reportedly damaged to the point that they could no longer safely be occupied. Structural problems became a major concern as families returned to inspect their properties. Residents described damaged walls, destroyed household items, and buildings that had become unsafe because of prolonged exposure to floodwater. Flood damage was also reported in urban areas. Zhou said some parts of Dunhua City experienced severe water accumulation, with some buildings seeing water levels rise significantly inside lower floors. Affected areas reportedly included Shaheyan Town, Dashitou Town, Heishi Township, Huangnihe Town, and E'mu Town. For many residents, the biggest concern was not only repairing homes but also recovering their ability to earn income. Farmers Face Severe Agricultural Losses The flooding caused major damage to agricultural production in the region. Residents said crops in fields were destroyed, creating additional financial pressure for farming families. For many rural households, agriculture and livestock provide their main source of income. Losing crops means losing both immediate earnings and future harvests. Zhou explained that families with savings may have more ability to recover, while elderly residents and households with limited financial resources could face much greater difficulties. The disaster has highlighted the economic vulnerability of rural communities when extreme weather events damage homes, farmland, and sources of income at the same time. Livestock Farmers Report Millions in Losses One of the most serious impacts was reported by livestock farmers in Dashitou Town. Han Chunmei, a livestock farmer in the area, said her farm lost hundreds of pigs during the flooding. She estimated that the financial damage reached several million yuan. According to Han’s account, rising water levels overwhelmed her farm, causing the deaths of most of her livestock. She said she had raised more than 800 pigs, but after the flood only a portion of the animals remained. Many piglets also died during the disaster. After the floodwaters withdrew, she described finding large numbers of animal carcasses around the farm area. Livestock losses can create long-term problems because farmers must deal not only with lost animals but also with cleanup costs, disease prevention concerns, and the challenge of restarting operations. Local Businesses Also Experience Major Damage The flooding affected more than farms. Residents said many local businesses suffered losses, including factories, restaurants, and other small enterprises. Dashitou Town reportedly has many livestock operations as well as businesses connected to local industries. Flood damage disrupted economic activity throughout the area. Residents said damaged equipment, destroyed inventory, and contaminated facilities could make recovery difficult for business owners. For families who rely on small businesses or farming, rebuilding may require significant financial support. Concerns Over Disaster Assistance and Recovery Support Residents interviewed about the flooding expressed concerns about the availability of disaster assistance. Han said she had heard reports of government relief funding but claimed she had not personally received direct assistance. She also said she attempted to seek attention online by sharing videos about the damage. According to her account, she later received requests to remove those posts. The claims made by individual residents could not be independently verified from the information available in the original report. However, their experiences reflect the frustration some disaster victims may feel when waiting for recovery support after a major emergency. Long Recovery Ahead for Flood-Affected Communities The flooding in Jilin Province has left many residents facing a difficult recovery period. Repairing damaged homes, restoring farmland, replacing lost livestock, and rebuilding businesses could take considerable time and resources. For rural communities especially, recovery is closely connected to restoring economic activity. Without adequate support, families who have lost homes and income sources may face continued hardship. As communities continue cleanup efforts, the long-term impact of the flooding will depend on reconstruction efforts, financial assistance, and measures taken to reduce future flood risks. Source NTD Television / The Epoch Times , including interviews with residents of Dunhua City and surrounding areas in Jilin Province. Disclaimer This rewritten article is provided for informational purposes only. The accounts and claims described are based on the source material provided and have not been independently verified by the author. Information regarding damages, government response, and individual experiences may change as additional reports become available.

title: NEW JERSEY NATURAL GAS ADVANCES COMMITMENT TO COST-EFFECTIVE EMISSIONS REDUCTION WITH THE INSTALLATION OF INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY FROM CARBON REFORM
summary: First Utility in New Jersey to Utilize This Breakthrough Carbon-Capture Technology
body_text: New Jersey Natural Gas NEW JERSEY NATURAL GAS ADVANCES COMMITMENT TO COST-EFFECTIVE EMISSIONS REDUCTION WITH THE INSTALLATION OF INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY FROM CARBON REFORM 07/24/2025 - For Immediate Release Wall, N.J. (July 24, 2025) – New Jersey Natural Gas (NJNG), the principal subsidiary of New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR), today announced the installation of Carbon Reform’s Carbon Reduction System to help advance its building decarbonization efforts. This new system at the NJNG Lakewood operations center is the first in New Jersey and highlights NJNG’s commitment to advancing innovation and practical, cost-effective solutions to reduce emissions. Carbon Reform’s Carbon Reduction System is a first-of-a-kind retrofit solution that utilizes permanent carbon capture to cut building emissions. The System’s broad capabilities can deliver other key benefits to commercial properties including reduced energy costs and increased overall efficiency. “NJNG is committed to identifying innovative technologies that provide practical, cost-effective solutions to emissions reduction for our customers,” said Patrick Migliaccio, senior vice president and COO of New Jersey Natural Gas. “The installation of Carbon Reform’s system at NJNG helps showcase the opportunity for this emerging technology and provides real-world insight on how these units perform. This milestone is another example of NJNG’s leadership in emissions reduction and sustainability.” The system’s latest Carbon Capsule® model introduces a modular design with custom color and sizing options to fit specific space requirements. As the company's lowest energy model yet, the Carbon Capsule® V3 provides buildings with an efficient and adaptable solution to reduce emissions that seamlessly integrates with existing HVAC systems. "Our work with New Jersey Natural Gas demonstrates how utilities can play a crucial role in bringing sustainable technologies directly to communities,” said Jo Norris, CEO and co-founder of Carbon Reform. “Together, we're showing that carbon-reduction technology can deliver other efficiencies, supporting more cost-effective building operations in a pragmatic way. We're excited to work with NJNG to demonstrate these benefits to New Jersey businesses." "The commercial building sector represents a significant opportunity for practical decarbonization solutions,” said Nick Martin, COO and co-founder of Carbon Reform. “Our work with utilities like New Jersey Natural Gas demonstrates how building operators can achieve meaningful emissions reductions while maintaining focus on their bottom line. This deployment will showcase how the broad capabilities of our technology, pairing carbon capture with air purification functionality, integrate seamlessly with existing building systems to improve efficiency and reduce energy costs with measurable results.” NJNG continues to pursue carbon-capture projects as part of NJR’s broader decarbonization goals and commitment to building a cleaner energy future driven by sustainability and reliability. Highlights of this progress include: Deployed over $71.3 million in SAVEGREEN® energy-efficiency programs to help customers reduce emissions. NJNG became the first utility in the state to install and operate distributed carbon-capture technology. NJR completed its first capped landfill community solar facility in New Jersey. NJR was named one of America’s Most Responsible Companies for 2024 by Newsweek – earning the recognition for the fifth consecutive year. NJR’s employees and retirees provided over 4,200 hours of volunteer service and its charitable foundations provided over $2.1 million in direct funding to local nonprofits. To read more about NJR’s sustainability efforts, visit njrsustainability.com . About New Jersey Resources: New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) is a Fortune 1000 company that, through its subsidiaries, provides safe and reliable natural gas and clean energy services, including transportation, distribution, asset management and home services. NJR is composed of five primary businesses: New Jersey Natural Gas , NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties. Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects, providing customers with low-carbon solutions. Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America. Storage and Transportation serves customers from local distributors and producers to electric generators and wholesale marketers through its ownership of Leaf River Energy Center and the Adelphia Gateway Pipeline, as well as our 50% equity ownership in the Steckman Ridge natural gas storage facility. Home Services provides service contracts as well as heating, central air conditioning, water heaters, standby generators, solar and other indoor and outdoor comfort products to residential homes throughout New Jersey. For more information about NJR, visit www.njresources.com . Follow us on X.com @NJNaturalGas . “Like” us on facebook.com/NewJerseyNaturalGas . About Carbon Reform Carbon Reform is a climate technology company founded in 2020 that develops innovative solutions for commercial building decarbonization. Based in Philadelphia and Delaware, Carbon Reform's team of engineers, scientists, and innovators creates technology that makes carbon removal and air quality improvements accessible while reducing building energy costs. title: How to Keep a Character Consistent in Flux
summary: Flux holds a character best with Flux Kontext, an in-context editing model that preserves a subject across edits with no training. For a fully repeatable identity, train a Flux LoRA; for faces in a busy frame, add PuLID.
body_text: HOW IT WORKS STEP 1 START FROM ONE CLEAN CHARACTER IMAGE Generate or choose a clear image of your character. With Kontext, this single image is the subject you preserve. STEP 2 EDIT IN CONTEXT WITH KONTEXT Load Flux Kontext, provide the character image plus an instruction like a new pose or scene. Kontext keeps the subject while changing the setting. STEP 3 TRAIN A LORA FOR FULL REPEATABILITY For a character you reuse constantly, train a Flux LoRA on 15 to 30 varied images and a unique trigger token, then call it in any prompt. STEP 4 TIGHTEN THE FACE WITH PULID When the face is small or drifting, add PuLID to preserve the specific identity on top of your prompt or LoRA. STEP 5 BRING IT TO LIFE IN FLICK Flux makes stills only. Drop your locked character into Flick and animate it with Veo 3, Kling, or Seedance so it carries into video.

title: GSK’s licensor Hansoh Pharma announces positive results from a second phase III trial for Ris-Rez in China
summary: ARTEMIS-011, a phase III study conducted for China, met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival in relapsed osteosarcoma
body_text: 28 July 2026 Issued: London, UK For media and investors only GSK’s licensor Hansoh Pharma announces positive results from a second phase III trial for Ris-Rez in China Download (PDF - 149.4KB) ARTEMIS-011, a phase III study conducted for China, met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival in relapsed osteosarcoma Results add to a growing body of positive late-stage evidence for Ris-Rez, including recent pivotal data in advanced or relapsed small-cell lung cancer GSK is advancing development of Ris-Rez outside China across multiple tumour types, including lung cancer, prostate cancer and other solid tumours GSK plc (LSE/NYSE: GSK) licensor Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. today announced that ARTEMIS-011, its pivotal phase III trial evaluating risvutatug rezetecan (Ris-Rez) in patients with osteosarcoma who have progressed or relapsed after receiving at least two prior lines of systemic therapy, met its primary endpoint of progression-free survival (PFS). In the trial, conducted in patients in China, Ris-Rez, a B7-H3-targeted antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), demonstrated statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in PFS compared with chemotherapy. Consistent benefit was also observed across secondary endpoints, including overall survival. The safety profile of ARTEMIS-011 is consistent with prior findings in this tumour type, and no new safety signals were identified. These data will be used by Hansoh Pharma for regulatory submission in China. GSK is advancing EMBOLD Sarcoma-202, a global phase Ib/II trial of Ris-Rez in previously treated unresectable advanced or metastatic sarcomas, including osteosarcoma. The study is part of GSK’s broader clinical development programme across multiple solid tumours, including lung and prostate cancers, under its exclusive global rights to develop Ris-Rez outside mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan. Ris-Rez has US FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation in relapsed or refractory osteosarcoma. Today’s results from Hansoh follow recently reported pivotal data in advanced or relapsed small-cell lung cancer (SCLC), making Ris-Rez the only B7-H3-targeted ADC to deliver positive phase III outcomes across multiple tumour types. Hesham Abdullah, Senior Vice President, Global Head Oncology, R&D, GSK said: "Building on recent pivotal data in small-cell lung cancer, these results strengthen our confidence in the broad potential of Ris-Rez and validate B7-H3 as a promising target across multiple tumour types." Osteosarcoma mainly affects children and young adults and is the most common primary bone cancer, accounting for 20-40% of all bone cancers1. It is a rare bone cancer with a global incidence of approximately 3.4 cases per million people per year2. Following first-line chemotherapy, treatment options for patients with relapsed osteosarcoma are severely limited, with no clear standard of care available3. After patients progress on two prior lines of treatment, options become even more limited, with no approved therapies. About risvutatug rezetecan Ris-Rez is a novel investigational B7-H3-targeted ADC composed of a fully human anti-B7-H3 monoclonal antibody covalently linked to a topoisomerase inhibitor payload. GSK acquired exclusive worldwide rights (excluding China’s mainland, Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan) from Hansoh Pharma to progress clinical development and commercialisation of Ris-Rez. Regulatory designations received for Ris-Rez to date include orphan drug designations from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in SCLC and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) in a category of cancer that includes SCLC, called pulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma; Priority Medicines (PRIME) Designation from the EMA for relapsed or refractory extensive-stage SCLC (ES-SCLC); and Breakthrough Therapy Designations for relapsed or refractory ES-SCLC and relapsed or refractory osteosarcoma from the US FDA.4,5,6,7,8,9,10 GSK in oncology Our ambition in oncology is to help increase overall quality of life, maximise survival and change the course of disease, expanding from our current focus on blood and women’s cancers into lung and gastrointestinal cancers, as well as other solid tumours. This includes accelerating priority programmes such as antibody-drug conjugates Ris Rez targeting B7-H3 and Mo-Rez targeting B7-H4, and velzatinib, a highly selective KIT tyrosine kinase inhibitor. About GSK GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. Find out more at www.gsk.com . title: Meet Anvil: The Coding Agent That Lives Where We Work
summary: How Concourse built Anvil, an autonomous engineering teammate that lives in Linear and Slack, runs on Claude Managed Agents, and carries work from request to a reviewable result.
body_text: Coding agents changed where work begins Anvil did more than help engineers write code faster. It changed how engineering work starts . A task might begin as a well-defined Linear issue, complete with acceptance criteria and links. Or it might begin as a half-formed question in Slack: “Can you look into this?”, “Could we build an integration for that?”, or “Why is this happening in production?” In either case, the handoff is the same. Assign the issue to Anvil or mention it in the conversation, and Anvil takes responsibility for the execution: gathering context, exploring the relevant systems, making a change when needed, running the appropriate checks, and bringing a concrete result back to the team, whether that is an answer, an RFC, or a pull request. There is no separate agent workspace people have to remember to visit. No new queue to monitor. No need to copy a Slack conversation into another tool and rebuild the context from scratch. Delegating to Anvil happens in the same places where we already delegate work to each other. That small interface decision changed how the agent was used. In its first few months, the results were hard to ignore: 700+ sessions initiated 40% of our Linear issues delegated to Anvil 300+ PRs merged to production (166 in June alone) Those numbers matter, but the more interesting story is why adoption happened. Coding ability was necessary, but it wasn't sufficient. The breakthrough was putting the agent between the structured world of Linear and the conversational world of Slack, and letting it carry work from an initial request to a concrete, reviewable result. The bridge between Linear and Slack Engineering work begins in two very different modes. The first is structured . A task has been discussed, scoped, and turned into an issue. It has an owner, a status, acceptance criteria, and a permanent place in the team's backlog. For us, that system of record is Linear. The second is conversational . Someone notices a problem, asks a question, shares an idea, or starts debugging in a Slack thread. The request may not be fully formed yet, and important context emerges through replies, links, corrections, and follow-up questions. Both modes are essential, but coding agents are often introduced through only one of them. An agent that lives exclusively in an issue tracker receives clean, structured tasks but can miss the conversation that produced them. An agent that lives exclusively in chat can join that conversation, but the work can disappear into a thread without durable ownership, status, or follow-through. Anvil connects the two. Anvil listens in Linear and Slack, runs the work on managed infrastructure, and acts across the tools the team already uses: GitHub, Notion, and Linear itself. When a Linear issue is assigned to Anvil, the issue becomes the starting point. Anvil reads its description and linked context, explores the relevant code, makes the change, runs the appropriate checks, opens a pull request, and moves the issue forward. When Anvil is mentioned in Slack, it begins with the conversation instead. It can answer a question, investigate a problem, do research, or start a complete engineering task using the context already in the thread. If the request turns into substantial work, the conversation can become a tracked Linear issue rather than staying buried in chat. From there the work continues through the normal engineering systems. Linear preserves ownership and status. GitHub holds the resulting code and pull request. Slack remains the place where people ask questions, clarify intent, and see what happened. The bridge is not simply copying messages between applications. It is carrying context across different modes of work. Slack is where intent is discovered and ambiguity is resolved. Linear is where a commitment becomes visible and accountable. GitHub is where the implementation becomes a reviewable artifact. Anvil connects those stages so the team does not have to reconstruct the task at every handoff. That is what makes delegation feel natural. People do not have to decide they are going to “use an AI tool.” They assign an issue or ask for help in a conversation, exactly as they would with another member of the team. Four ways we use it 1 · Shipping a real migration We handed Anvil a genuine backend migration as an ordinary Linear issue: move a workflow build off one-shot HTTP requests and onto a durable execution model. Anvil read the ticket and its linked context, explored the relevant code, made the change across the files involved, ran the checks, and opened a pull request. Eight files changed, one PR, and the issue moved to Done. This was meaningful, multi-file engineering work, not a cosmetic edit or a demo task. A migration delegated as a Linear issue: started by Anvil, eight files changed, PR opened, marked Done. 2 · Turning a Slack thread into shipped work This one started as a single message in a channel: “can you build a new integration? let's make it live.” The requirements weren't fully formed yet; they took shape through the replies that followed. Anvil used that evolving thread as its context, then turned the request into tracked work and, ultimately, a pull request. The conversation where the intent emerged stayed connected to the engineering result, instead of the request and its outcome becoming two disconnected pieces of work. Kicking off integration work with a single Slack mention, then iterating in the reply thread. 3 · Researching before committing to code Here the handoff was an open-ended question rather than a defined task: how could we make configurations swappable at runtime? Anvil investigated the relevant systems in parallel and synthesized what it found. The result wasn't code but a full RFC document the team could read, question, and refine before anyone committed to an implementation. The artifact gave the team something concrete to evaluate before a line of code was written. From an open question to a written RFC: research delegated end to end. 4 · Starting an investigation from your phone The request came in from a phone, away from any laptop: “How many agents have we run in production today?” Anvil queried our observability data, cross-checked more than one source, and came back with an actual number and the caveats around it, not a link to a dashboard. The unlock is immediacy: an engineer can begin a real investigation from anywhere, without waiting to get back to a desk or manually navigating several observability tools. “How many agents have we run in production today?” Answered from a phone, with the agent pulling and cross-checking live observability data. We chose where to build Anvil needed an environment where an agent could work for more than a single response. It needed to read files, run commands, execute code, use tools, browse the web, and maintain state while completing longer tasks. We could have built that infrastructure ourselves. We chose not to. Anvil runs on Claude Managed Agents , which provides the agent harness and managed execution environment. It gives Anvil a place to perform long-running work, use tools, interact with files, and maintain a session while it works toward an outcome. That let us focus on the layer that was specific to our team. We built the layer around that runtime: how requests enter through Linear or Slack, how context follows them, how Anvil connects to the systems where engineering work happens, how tasks move through their lifecycle, and how results return to the people who delegated them. This distinction became central to how we thought about the product. The managed runtime provides the ability to execute. Anvil provides the workflow around that execution: where work begins, what context it receives, how people interact with it, where the resulting artifact belongs, and how the task reconnects with the team. Model capabilities and agent runtimes will keep improving. By building on that infrastructure rather than recreating it, those improvements become a tailwind. We can keep concentrating on the part that makes Anvil useful inside a real organization: turning an informal request into work that is visible, actionable, and easy to pick up again. The technology made autonomous execution possible. The bridge between Linear and Slack made it something people actually used. What we learned Distribution is part of the product An agent can be extremely capable and still go unused if people have to remember where it lives. Every additional step between noticing work and delegating it creates friction: opening another application, starting a session, copying context, rewriting the request, and later returning to check what happened. Putting Anvil in Linear and Slack removed most of those decisions. People encounter the agent at the moment the work appears, and adoption did not require learning a new workflow; it extended ones they already understood. For an internal agent, where it is available can matter as much as what it can do. Conversation and systems of record serve different purposes Slack and Linear are not competing interfaces for the same job. Slack captures emerging intent: the questions, links, disagreements, and incremental clarification through which a task takes shape. Linear preserves the resulting commitment by giving it ownership, priority, status, and a durable place in the plan. The lesson was not to choose one interface over the other. It was to let work change shape without losing its context. A conversation can become a commitment; that commitment can become a pull request or another concrete artifact. Anvil carries the work across those transitions rather than trying to replace the systems on either side. A useful agent returns an artifact The value of an agent session is not the length of the conversation or the number of actions it took. It is what the team can do with the result. For engineering work that usually means a pull request; for research, an RFC; for debugging, a sourced answer with enough evidence to make a decision. These artifacts give the work a life beyond the session. They can be reviewed, discussed, improved, shared, and accepted through the team's existing processes. That reframed Anvil for us: its job is not merely to respond intelligently, but to carry work forward and return something concrete. What comes next Anvil began with a simple bet: a coding agent becomes far more useful when delegating to it feels as natural as delegating to another person. The first phase was about closing the loop from request to result. A conversation in Slack or an issue in Linear could become an investigation, a document, or a pull request without someone manually carrying the context between every system. The next phase is about making that handoff more complete. We want Anvil to preserve context across longer timelines, resume work when new information or feedback arrives, and use the lessons from reviews and completed tasks to approach future work more effectively. The emphasis is not simply adding more places to invoke Anvil. It is making the work more continuous after the first handoff. The opportunity is to shrink the distance between noticing work and meaningfully starting it: to begin investigations while an engineer is away from their desk, turn ideas into tracked work before their context disappears, and return more tasks to the team as concrete artifacts ready for judgment. Writing code was the first capability. Building a reliable path from request to result is the larger opportunity. That is what we are building with Anvil. Anvil · built at Concourse
